nm_shady_side_left.blurb: The leftmost stretch of the Shady Side cliff near Alamogordo, and the first piece of rock a party meets on the way in. All 24 routes are bolted sport climbs, and the difficulty is high: a few in the low 5.11s, a large block of 5.12s and 5.13s, and a single 5.14. The left half is very steep and bouldery, with only a couple of hard moves between plentiful jugs, while the right side lies back to vertical and slabby ground that asks for more technique. The face is exposed, so carrying a stick clip makes sense. Shade is the draw here, which suits warm days. This is not a spot for climbers still working through moderate grades.

nm_07_randy_s_wall.blurb: A mostly bolted wall on the upper cliff band of Palomas Peak in the Sandia mountains. Of its 24 routes, about twenty are sport, with a pair of top-ropes and a pair of trad lines. Grades run from 5.7 up to 5.12, with a fairly even spread through 5.9 to 5.12, so mid-grade climbers have plenty to choose from. The limestone is sharp and heavily textured, giving near-vertical slabs that call for smearing, stemming and laybacks, plus a few thin cracks. Expect hard wear on skin and shoes, and bring tape for the cracks.
nm_07_randy_s_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the row of three concrete barriers beside the dirt road. There is space for about eight or nine cars parked end-on, with a few more spots a short way along. Carpooling helps.
nm_07_randy_s_wall.approach: Follow the trail from the barriers for roughly 0.7 mile to a signed junction, turn hard left and climb about a quarter mile to the cliff band, then continue along its base to the wall. Allow around half an hour with a full pack.

nm_09_the_far_side_ii.blurb: A section near the far north end of the upper cliff band on Palomas Peak, in the Sandia mountains. Most of the 24 routes are bolted sport, with a handful of trad lines on the dihedrals and cracks. Grades go from 5.8 to 5.12, centred on 5.10, which makes it a good stop for intermediate climbers. The limestone offers long, moderate face climbing. The lowest stretch of the cliff is loose and chossy and breaks off easily, particularly after rain, so watch your footing at the start of routes.
nm_09_the_far_side_ii.parking_note: Leave the car at the row of three concrete barriers beside the dirt road. There is space for about eight or nine cars parked end-on, with a few more spots a short way along. Carpooling helps.
nm_09_the_far_side_ii.approach: Follow the trail from the barriers for roughly 0.7 mile to a signed junction, turn hard left and climb about a quarter mile to the cliff band, then walk north along its base to the wall. Allow around half an hour with a full pack.

nm_las_hermanas.blurb: Three big boulders, each around 40 feet tall, in the southern part of the Box climbing area west of Socorro. The 24 climbs are a mix: more than half are boulder problems from easy up to hard, with several in the V2 to V5 range, plus about eight bolted sport routes and a couple of trad lines running from easy fifth class to 5.12. The moves are typical for Socorro, technical and crimpy with the odd pocket, on rock that goes from slabby to slightly overhanging. A good stop if you want to mix bouldering with a few short roped climbs.

_expect.name: Filet de Papillon Wall (aka Dirt Wall)

nm_filet_de_papillon_wall_aka_dirt_wall.blurb: A west-facing wall in the northern Box area near Socorro, with a shallow cave at its left end. Nearly all of the 24 climbs are fully bolted sport routes, plus one boulder problem in the cave. Routes are long for the area and lean hard: one easy-ish line near 5.8, a few in the 5.10s and low 5.11s, then a big group of 5.12s and a handful at 5.13 and above. It is a destination for strong sport climbers rather than beginners, and the walk from the canyon floor is short.
